Reef Station 07 · kelp canyon · 18 m · dawn dive

Pelagic Drift

message.reasoning:
Need to deliver a single self-contained HTML file with SVG underwater scene. Let me build it carefully. The task demands it all. I want it to feel alive and crafted. I'll lean into an ambient layered background, several moving elements, hover/scroll micro-interactions, and strong contrast in type sizes/weights, plus a distinctive display face paired with a readable body face. But no external assets — fonts must be system/local stacks. A distinctive display look can come from font stacks like "Didot, 'Playfair Display'..." hmm, no CDN. Use local fonts: e.g., display: 'Georgia'/'Iowan Old Style'/'Palatino' vs body: system sans. Or a condensed sans stack: "'Haettenschweiler','Arial Narrow'". For a marine-log aesthetic maybe a monospace-ish stack for labels and a serif display. That gives character without network. File size under 18 KB — keep it lean but rich. Careful with size. Plan: - SVG full viewport, viewBox based on window size, updated on resize. Use preserveAspectRatio="none"? Better: use pixel-based coordinate system equal to viewport (width = innerWidth, height = innerHeight), updating on resize. - Layers: water gradient background rect, light rays (god rays) as translucent polygons animated, distant particulates (marine snow), seafloor path (sand + rocks), seaweed (wavy paths with sway via transform rotate animation on groups anchored at base, or animate path d — simpler: CSS transform-origin at base with rotate keyframes; but CSS transform on SVG elements works with transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: bottom center. Good. - Fish: 2 groups built from primitives, driven by JS requestAnimationFrame for horizontal movement with wrap-around, with vertical bobbing and tail wiggle (rotate tail group), body slight yaw. - Bubbles: JS-managed, spawn from seafloor vents, rise with drift, recycle at top. At least 5 — I'll do ~14. - Micro-interactions: hover on fish → brief speed-up / highlight ring? Pointer interactions: clicking somewhere spawns a small burst of bubbles; mouse move creates a subtle light shift (caustics follow pointer). Hovering seaweed makes it sway more. A small UI HUD in corner: title "ABYSSAL DRIFT / Station 07 — Kelp Canyon" with type contrast, plus a legend listing the two fish with tiny SVG icons; hover legend item highlights the corresponding fish (dim the others / show label line). That's the interactive richness. Careful: hover interaction needs pointer-events management — the SVG background shouldn't block? Actually we want clicks on water to spawn bubbles; put a full-size rect for that or use svg listener. Also need to keep file < 18KB. Let's be economical: inline CSS compact, JS compact but readable. Let me design the scene coordinates: W = innerWidth, H = innerHeight. Seafloor at y = H - floorH where floorH ≈ 0.13*H. Fish A: large, round/short body — a sunfish-ishMola-like disc: big ellipse body with tall triangular dorsal and anal fins, stubby triangular tail, single visible eye with pupil, mouth line. Colors: warm — a coral fish against a blue field reads instantly and gives the palette punch; let's do coral/orange with amber belly and cream fins. Hmm orange on blue is complementary — good contrast, and it's the classic clownfish/fanfish read. Fish B: small, slender elongated — torpedo body (path or ellipse with high rx/ry ratio), long pointed tail, single dorsal fin, blue/white striped — teal/silver. Clearly smaller. Sizes: Fish A body ~ rx 84 ry 58 → total length ~230. Fish B body rx 52 ry 17 → total ~130. Different. Fish construction details: Fish A (big round, "Sunfish"): - group with translate(x,y) scale(sx,1) where sx=±1 based on direction. - tail: polygon triangle at rear, animated rotate around attach point. - body: ellipse cx0 cy0 rx 82 ry 56, fill radialGradient (coral → deep). - tail for round fish at rear x=-82: triangle points (-78,0) (-150,-46) (-150,46). Fine. - dorsal fin top: path with curves, a triangular-ish tall fin on top of body. - pectoral fin: small ellipse/path rotating slightly. - eye: circle white/pale at (36,-14) r 13, pupil circle r 5.5 at (39,-14) r 5.5, plus tiny highlight dot r 1.8. - mouth: path curve near x=78. - stripes: 3 arcs as decoration (paths, allowed). - lip: small ellipse. Fish B (small slender, "Lancer"): - tail triangle at rear, longer pointed. - body: path teardrop/slender: use ellipse rx 54 ry 16 plus pointed snout path. Or path: M -50,0 C -30,-18 30,-16 58,0 C 30,16 -30,18 -50,0 Z. Nice slender lens shape. - dorsal fin small triangle on top; a side fin. - eye at (36,-4) r 7.5 with pupil r 3.2. - mouth: line. - stripes: vertical thin rects clipped? Use paths with a clipPath of body. Wrap-around: each fish has x position; when x > W + margin → x = -margin (moving right) etc. Direction: both swim horizontally. One fish goes right faster, other left slower (different speeds, noticeably). Add vertical bob with sine, and slight pitch. Also flip: fish moving left face left; the shapes are drawn facing right, so scale(-1,1) for leftward. Bubble loop: array of {x, y, r, vy, drift, phase}. Update: y -= vy*dt, x += sin(phase + t)*drift. When y < -r*2 → respawn at a random vent near seafloor. vy inversely proportional to r (smaller rise faster). Use a group with circles; each bubble a containing circle + highlight circle for spherical look. Or single circle with radialGradient fill (fill="url(#bub)") plus a small white highlight ellipse. Cheaper: circle with fill url(#bub) stroke rgba white. Keep 16 bubbles: each a , transform translate. Actually to reduce DOM churn, generate them in JS. Seaweed: 3 clusters (kelp) each a wavy path with stroke, stroke-linecap round, plus leaf ellipses. Sway via CSS animation with different durations and delays. Also some sea-grass blades and a rock or two, anemone maybe. Keep count. Light rays: 4 polygons with gradient fill, animated opacity/skew via CSS keyframes; slowly drifting. Caustics: subtle animated ellipses at top with blur? feGaussianBlur filter is allowed (inline SVG). A filter on a group can be expensive but fine. I'll skip filters or use one small blur on light rays maybe. Use opacity gradients instead to keep perf. Marine snow: ~30 tiny dots drifting slowly, JS or CSS. I'll do CSS-animated small circles with random positions generated by JS. Keep it cheap: 24 dots. HUD: top-left title, small typographic block with display serif ("ABYSSAL"?) Let me theme it as a field-log/dive-slate. Type: display = "Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif"? That's a bit generic. Better distinctive: 'Hoefler Text', 'Iowan Old Style', 'Palatino Linotype', 'Book Antiqua', Georgia, serif — a serif display on deep blue reads elegant and distinctive. Body/labels: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace for the slate/telemetry feel. Good pairing: serif display + mono body — it reads like a dive slate rather than a generic sans. HUD content: a dive-slate panel with title "PELAGIC", subtitle, and a species register with two rows, each showing a mini SVG fish icon (primitives), name, size, speed readout live-updating (speed in px/s). Hover row → highlight fish in scene (add class to fish group → scale up slightly + glow ring + label line). Click row → maybe pulse. Scroll reveals: it's full viewport no scroll — instead do load-in reveals (staggered fade/slide of HUD elements). And on resize recompute. Also mouse parallax: shift background layers slightly with pointer. Bubble spawn on click at pointer: spawn 6 bubbles at click point (nice micro-interaction). Also fish curious about pointer? Could add: fish veer toward cursor slightly — but the requirement is horizontal wrap; keep vertical bob plus tiny attraction. Keep it simple: on click, fish briefly dart faster (speed boost). Nice. Let's ensure exactly 2 fish and 1 visible eye each (only one side shown). Yes. Now, size budget. Let's write it carefully and compactly. Aim ~13–16KB. Structure: ```html Pelagic Drift — Reef Station 07
HUD
``` SVG sizing: width:100vw;height:100vh;display:block; set viewBox via JS to `0 0 W H`. Use attribute width/height 100%. Resize handler recomputes positions: floorY, seaweed paths regenerate, fish y positions, bubbles. Better approach: build the dynamic geometry (floor path, seaweed, rays) in JS so they adapt to viewport. Fish defined statically in markup with transform set by JS. Yes — build floor/weed/rays/bubbles in JS. That keeps HTML small. But then I must be careful. Let me write the JS: ```js const S=document.getElementById('stage'); let W=innerWidth,H=innerHeight,floor=H; function layout(){W=innerWidth;H=innerHeight;floor=H-Math.max(70,H*0.13);S.setAttribute('viewBox','0 0 '+W+' '+H);buildFloor();buildWeed();buildRays();} ``` buildFloor: a path across the bottom with gentle hills, sand gradient, plus a darker rock silhouette behind, plus scattered pebbles (ellipses), plus a couple of rocks (path polygons). Sand gradient linearGradient defined in defs with y1 floor-ish; gradients in userSpaceOnUse would need updating; simpler use objectBoundingBox gradient on the path (bbox = floor region) — that works nicely: gradient from #cbb98a to #6b5a3f. Seaweed: function kelp(x, h, amp, hue, w). Build path: from (x, floor) rising with sinusoidal lateral offset, as a filled tapered shape? A stroke path with varying widths: use multiple strokes of decreasing width. Simpler: a filled path with two edges. Let's do filled tapered blade: ``` function blade(x,h,amp,phase,wid,col){ const seg=7; let L='',R=''; for(let i=0;i<=seg;i++){ const t=i/seg, y=floor-h*t, xo=x+Math.sin(t*3.1+phase)*amp*t; const w=wid*(1-t*0.85); L+=(i?'L':'M')+xo.toFixed(1)+','+y.toFixed(1); } ... } ``` Simplify: stroke path with `stroke-width` and linecap round; that reads fine as wavy kelp strand. Plus small ellipse leaves along it. I'll do strokes (stroke gradient green) — "wavy path" satisfies the requirement literally. Good, cheaper. Path: M x,floor then cubic segments alternating direction: use quadratic chain. ``` let d='M'+x+','+floor; for(i=0;i<3;i++){ d+= ' Q'+(x+s*(0.4+i*0.3)*amp)+','+(floor-h*(i+0.33)/3*1)+' '+ (x + offset)...} ``` Let me just do polyline with many points using a sine, and stroke — smooth enough with 20 points; use 'Q' smoothing not needed. d = points joined by 'L' with 14 points along a sine — looks slightly jagged but with stroke-linejoin round it's fine. Better: use the sine with step and it's smooth. Use 16 points; amplitude grows with height. Fine. Kelp cluster: 4–6 blades at slightly different x, heights, phases; group has CSS animation: `animation: sway 7s ease-in-out infinite alternate; transform-origin: bottom center`? transform-origin on the group in SVG needs transform-box: fill-box → then bottom center of its bbox = base. Yes: `.weed{transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:50% 100%;animation:sway ...}`. But fill-box for a group with only strokes: bbox may exclude stroke but fine. Careful: if group transform is animated by CSS while I also set transform attribute for positioning — CSS transform overrides the attribute. So wrap: outer containing inner blades drawn in local coords. Blades local coords then x=0 base at y=floor. Good; sway rotates the inner group. Actually rotation about base of tall kelp gives nice sway. Combine rotate + a slight skew. Keyframes: rotate(-3deg) → rotate(4deg). Anemone/coral accents: a few small fans (ellipse fan) on the floor for richness. And a "distant kelp forest" silhouette band (dark blurred vertical wavy strokes at low opacity behind everything, near bottom). Good depth. Rays: polygons from top narrow to wide bottom, fill url(#ray), opacity animated, and translateX drift via CSS. 5 rays positioned as fraction of W. Since W set by JS, build rays in JS with coordinates from W. Snow/marine particles: JS creates 26 circles with random x,y in the whole water region and CSS animation drift+fade, durations randomized via inline style. Caustic light at top: a rect with a radial gradient? I'll add 3 wide ellipses at top with low-opacity white and slow horizontal drift, using CSS transform translate. Skip blur filter (perf). Maybe use one small blur on the rays group only. Fine. Vignette: radial gradient rect overlay, pointer-events none. Fish markup (static, in SVG): ```html ... label line + text ... (hidden until hover) ``` Hmm: fish group transform set by JS each frame: `translate(x,y) scale(dir,1) rotate(pitch)`. Text label inside would be mirrored when dir=-1. Put the label in a separate group positioned by JS separately (id f1tag) in a tags layer. Or simpler: HUD hover highlights the fish with a glow (feDropShadow? use a stroke halo circle). I'll do: on hover of a register row, the fish group gets class 'spot' → an (a dashed circle) appears and rotates, plus fish scales 1.06. Implement halo as a circle inside the unmirrored wrapper... The mirror is applied via scale(dir,1) on an inner group; outer group only translates. So structure: `...shapes...`. Halo in outer group → no mirroring. Let's do that: JS sets f1.setAttribute('transform', `translate(${x},${y})`) and flip.setAttribute('transform', `scale(${dir},1) rotate(${pitch})`). Tail wiggle: set on tail group transform: `rotate(${angle}, px, py)` with angle = sin(t*speed)*14 around pivot. Or use CSS animation for tail (simpler and frame-cheap): `.tail{animation:kick .55s ease-in-out infinite alternate; transform-box:fill-box;transform-origin:100% 50%}` where tail is drawn with its attach at right (front of tail is the body side). For a fish facing right, tail is at the left, so its attach point is the right edge of its bbox → transform-origin:100% 50%. Good, CSS handles it. Different durations per fish (bigger fish slower tail beat). Pectoral fin: CSS rotate gentle. Gill flutter? skip. Fish vertical bob: JS sin. Also add a shadow-ish darker ellipse under fish? skip. Now speed: requirement "Each fish must move at a noticeably different speed". Big fish 46 px/s, small fish 118 px/s. Directions: big one drifts right slowly, little one darts left faster? Also both wrap. Let's do big → right (dir +1), small → left (dir -1) so their paths cross; adds life. Show live speed readout in HUD (updates ~5/s). Extra life: a school of tiny distant fish silhouettes drifting (adds ambient). Could be nice but risks "exactly 2 fish" check failing — the requirement says exactly 2 fish. Silhouettes might count as fish. Avoid. Instead use jellyfish? Also a creature; risky but they're not fish... A checker (automated or human) counts fish-shaped things. Safer: no other animals. Just particles, rays, bubbles, kelp, rocks. HUD (dive slate), bottom-left: ```

Instead give base r=10 and scale s = r/10; stroke non-scaling? Use vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke". Good trick: stroke-width .8 with vector-effect non-scaling-stroke. So one shared geometry per bubble: ``. Scale group by r/10. Bubble rise: vy = (14 + 26/ (r/6)) px/s? smaller rise faster: v = 26 + 120/(r) ... choose v = 18 + 42/ (r/3) hmm. Let's: v = 22 + 260/r (r in px, 2..7). r=2 → 152 px/s (too fast maybe). Let's v = 20 + 90/r → r=2 → 65, r=6 → 35, r=7 → 33. Reasonable, small faster. Multiply by a random 0.85..1.2. Let's fill with a linearGradient vertical: #ffd9a0 top → #f2793b mid → #b83f2c bottom. Plus a highlight path on top. - Actually "round/short": rx=88 ry=66. Tail small relative. - tail group at x from -84: polygon points "-84,0 -168,-56 -168,56" — a big triangle but for sunfish the tail is a stubby keel; use "-84,0 -150,-44 -150,44" plus rounded? Triangle required by spec ("triangular tail"). Fine. - dorsal fin: top triangle-ish path: "M -18,-60 C -2,-124 42,-118 56,-52 Z" — a tall sweeping fin. Fill darker orange with translucent. - anal fin bottom mirror: "M -14,60 C 0,112 34,108 48,52 Z". - pectoral fin: ellipse at (18,16) rx 26 ry 13 rotated -20, with gentle rotate animation, fill rgba cream .55. - eye: center (52,-22) r 14 fill #fff8ec; pupil circle (56,-22) r 6.5 fill #17222e; glint circle (58.5,-25) r 2 fill #fff. - mouth: path "M 84,-4 q 10,4 6,14" hmm mouth at front (x≈+86). Stripe paths: "M -20,-70 C -6,-20 -6,20 -20,70" etc with stroke rgba(255,255,255,.16) width 9. - Also gill line arc: path "M 34,-56 C 22,-16 22,16 34,54" stroke rgba(0,0,0,.12) width 5. - Freckles dots: a few circles. Keep triangle: "-54,0 -108,-28 -108,28". - dorsal: path "M -8,-15 C 2,-40 22,-38 30,-13 Z". - side fin: small path near (14,8). - eye: circle (38,-4) r 8 fill #eafeff; pupil r 3.6 fill #0b2430; glint r 1.3. - mouth: line path "M 58,2 q 6,3 2,7"?
